key_insight: CAVQS reduces two-qubit gate counts by optimizing across circuit-block boundaries and exploiting permitted terminal measurements with classical feedforward.
engineering_relevance: Lower CNOT counts can ease quantum hardware demands, while dynamic implementations require measurement and feedforward support.
method: Use QR decomposition to redistribute unitary factors between overlapping blocks while preserving the overall transformation.
Reshape local synthesis targets to enable cross-block gate reductions.
For eligible terminal-measurement blocks, combine CNOT-budgeted search with analytic branch-unitary construction to minimize expected CNOT cost without ancillas.
evidence_signal: On common successful random-circuit instances, mean two-qubit gate reductions were 28.79–42.52% versus QFAST, 2.05–52.62% versus SQUANDER, and 30.51–74.64% versus Fast-USYN; reductions on 4–6-qubit algorithm benchmarks ranged from 20.65% to 71.88% across these baselines.
watch_item: Gate-count savings do not establish hardware-level speed or fidelity gains, particularly when measurement and feedforward latency matter.
paper_title: CAVQS: Context-Aware Variational Quantum Circuit Synthesis via Unitary Redistribution and Dynamic Reconstruction
